title: Kernel core adversarial matrix
note: Every element in docs/architecture/KERNEL-CONSTITUTION.md sections 1-6 must correspond to at least one case here (the document's own Testability rule). 15 cases total, per the Phase-2 one-shot spec's required minimum: 8 EXECUTED/SIMULATED this phase via benchmarks/e5-02-unknown-outcome/, 7 NOT_EXECUTED with stated reasons. A case with no corresponding test is not yet a tested part of the constitution, regardless of how precisely it is described in prose.

cases.name: duplicate-operation
cases.expected_state: Second dispatch with the same idempotency key never re-performs the effect; operation resolves ACKED from the first attempt's evidence.
cases.expected_evidence: Service-side dispatch_attempts counter increments without a new committed_at.
cases.expected_recovery: N/A - no crash involved, purely a duplicate-call path.
cases.actual_result: pass: true - service deduped, committed_at unchanged, dispatch_attempts incremented once

cases.name: timeout-after-real-side-effect
cases.expected_state: DISPATCHED -> UNKNOWN_OUTCOME (never REJECTED) when the kernel stops waiting on a still-running dispatch.
cases.expected_evidence: No ACKED/REJECTED evidence exists at the moment of timeout classification.
cases.expected_recovery: Reconciliation later resolves ACKED once the service's own log catches up.
cases.must_never_happen: A timeout is silently treated as REJECTED (the exact failure mode ADR-0011 exists to prevent).
cases.actual_result: pass: true - classified UNKNOWN_OUTCOME while service still running, resolved ACKED after

cases.name: response-lost-after-real-side-effect
cases.expected_state: DISPATCHED -> UNKNOWN_OUTCOME -> RECONCILING -> ACKED, isolated from the primary 12-step composite.
cases.expected_evidence: Service log shows the effect committed; kernel never observed a response.
cases.expected_recovery: Reconciliation queries the service's own durable log directly.
cases.must_never_happen: Reconciliation re-dispatches instead of querying first.
cases.actual_result: pass: true - sideEffectCommitted true, responseObserved false, resolved ACKED; flaked once during development (see E5-02-RESULT.md Corrections #4), fixed and reconfirmed clean across 5 re-runs

cases.name: kill-before-checkpoint
cases.expected_state: Crash between AUTHORIZED and the DISPATCHED checkpoint leaves the operation at AUTHORIZED, never DISPATCHED.
cases.expected_evidence: No service log entry exists for the operation's idempotency key.
cases.expected_recovery: Safe to dispatch fresh - no ambiguity, no reconciliation needed.
cases.must_never_happen: The operation is treated as UNKNOWN_OUTCOME when no dispatch was ever checkpointed.
cases.actual_result: pass: true - stateOnRestart AUTHORIZED, serviceHasRecordOfEffect false

cases.name: kill-after-checkpoint
cases.expected_state: DISPATCHED checkpoint is durable but the service call never actually reached the service.
cases.expected_evidence: No service log entry found on reconciliation.
cases.expected_recovery: Classify UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, then reconcile to REJECTED given no evidence.
cases.must_never_happen: REJECTED is assumed safe by default against a real external system with no reliable status check - it is not; this case's REJECTED result is trustworthy only because the SIMULATED service happens to offer one.
cases.actual_result: pass: true - classified UNKNOWN_OUTCOME, resolved REJECTED, serviceEvidenceFound false

cases.name: checkpoint-corruption
cases.expected_state: A corrupted kernel database is detected on open/read, never silently trusted.
cases.expected_evidence: PRAGMA integrity_check or an open failure signals the corruption.
cases.expected_recovery: Route to MANUAL_REVIEW (detection only in this harness; no repair/quarantine path implemented).
cases.must_never_happen: Corrupted state is read and acted on as if valid.
cases.actual_result: pass: true after correction - first corruption technique (mid-file byte overwrite) went UNDETECTED by PRAGMA integrity_check (an honest miss, corrected not hidden); header-magic-byte corruption reliably detected via threwOnOpen. Only corruption criterion 1 (schema violation) measured, not 2/3/5/6/7 (E5-RESULT.md's 7-criteria definition).

cases.name: replay-determinism
cases.expected_state: The same persisted state, reconciled twice from independent snapshots, produces byte-identical resulting state/outcome.
cases.expected_evidence: Two independent DB snapshots taken from the same source, reconciled separately.
cases.expected_recovery: N/A - determinism check, not a crash scenario.
cases.must_never_happen: Two replays of identical input produce different classifications (violates the determinism invariant in section 1).
cases.actual_result: pass: true - replayA and replayB identical (state ACKED, outcome ACKED)

cases.name: concurrent-state-mutation
cases.expected_state: Two independently spawned reconciliation workers race on the same UNKNOWN_OUTCOME operation; exactly one wins the guarded transition.
cases.expected_evidence: Optimistic-concurrency version check rejects the loser's write (0 rows affected).
cases.expected_recovery: The losing worker detects the loss and does not retry blindly within this harness.
cases.must_never_happen: Both workers succeed, or a duplicate dispatch is triggered by the race.
cases.actual_result: pass: true - exactlyOneWon true, noDuplicateDispatchTriggered true (2 real spawned processes, not simulated in-process)

cases.name: illegal-transition
cases.expected_state: A Guard rejects a transition attempt outside the legal state graph; this is a defined outcome, not a kernel failure.
cases.reason: This harness's transition() guard rejects any fromStates mismatch mechanically, but there is no real Guard/Context model (section 1) to mount an actually adversarial illegal-transition attempt against - only the one legal path per case was exercised, never a deliberate illegal one.
cases.trigger: A real state-machine implementation with an explicit Guard/Context model exists (Phase 4+).

cases.name: duplicate-event
cases.expected_state: An Event replayed twice (same Event identity) is detected as a duplicate, not applied twice.
cases.reason: No Event identity/log exists in this harness (section 1's Event carries its own identity) - only Operation-level idempotency was exercised, a distinct mechanism from Event-level deduplication.
cases.trigger: A real Event log/identity mechanism exists (Phase 4+).

cases.name: reordered-event
cases.expected_state: Events applied out of persisted order are detected or rejected, not silently accepted in the wrong order.
cases.reason: Same reason as duplicate-event: no persisted Event log exists in this harness to reorder.
cases.trigger: A real Event log/identity mechanism exists (Phase 4+).

cases.name: stale-authorization
cases.expected_state: A Capability grant past its expiry is rejected at enforcement time, not honored because it was valid at authorization time.
cases.reason: Capability/PolicyDecision fields are recorded but never expire or get re-evaluated in this harness - needs a real Capability grant with an expiry per ADR-0013.
cases.trigger: A real CapabilityEngine with grant expiry exists (Phase 8/9).

cases.name: capability-escalation
cases.expected_state: An attempt to act beyond a granted Capability's scope is rejected at the source-to-sink enforcement point.
cases.reason: No real Capability enforcement boundary exists yet (Phase 8/9 unstarted) - the capability field in this harness is a label recorded on the Operation row, not an enforced grant checked against the action taken.

cases.name: policy-bypass
cases.expected_state: An Operation cannot dispatch without an independently-evaluated, current Policy decision - a stale or absent PolicyDecision blocks dispatch.
cases.reason: Same reason as capability-escalation - PolicyDecision is recorded on the Operation row but never enforced by a real PolicyEngine that could reject dispatch.

cases.name: schema-version-mismatch
cases.expected_state: A Checkpoint written by schema version N remains readable by version N+1 (or fails explicitly with a migration path, never silently misreads).
cases.reason: This harness runs a single schema version throughout its whole run - no second real schema version exists yet to test migration/mismatch against (ADR-0010's schema migration invariant is a Phase 4 concern).
cases.trigger: Phase 4 CheckpointStore exists with a second real schema version to migrate against.

summary.sections_not_covered_note: Sections 5 and 6 are structural/organizational (Evidence/Verdict field shapes; layer ownership table) rather than state-transition behavior - no case in the one-shot spec's 15 targets them directly. Every EXECUTED case does produce Evidence and reach a Verdict-labeled terminal state as a side effect of running, but no case exists whose specific purpose is to adversarially test section 5 or 6's own rules (e.g. 'a Verdict with no cited Evidence is malformed' is asserted in the spec but never deliberately violated and checked in this harness). Logged here rather than silently left uncovered - a real gap for a future E5, not claimed as tested.
